mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, as observed over the last three weeks, indicates a return to office-based work, which will drive increased weekday retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES remaining positive and stable.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend, approaching pre-pandemic levels, it signals a shift towards more out-of-home activities, directly boosting retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or stagnates over the next 14 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below the 5.0% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent positive trends in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggest a robust return to urban commuting and daily routines, which will collectively stimulate retail and recreation spending over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing sustained positive trends.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden and significant week-on-week drop in RETAIL_REC mobility, especially after a period of stability, indicates the likely imposition of new public health restrictions, leading to a further decline in retail activity over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC drops by more than 1.0 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers or stabilizes within the next 7 days, despite a week-on-week drop exceeding 1.0 point.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained negative trend in PARKS mobility, indicating reduced outdoor leisure, suggests a broader reluctance for recreational activities, which will indirectly dampen overall retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, even if PARKS mobility remains consistently negative or declines further.

mechanism_narrative: Consistent high levels of GROCERY_PHARM mobility, well above baseline, signify robust essential activity and consumer confidence, which will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 14.0% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM consistently staying above 14.0%.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated while WORKPLACES mobility shows signs of stagnation or decline, it indicates a continued preference for home-based activities or reduced commuting, leading to decreased retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 5.0% AND WORKPLACES < 2.0% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, even when RESIDENTIAL mobility is high and WORKPLACES mobility is low.

mechanism_narrative: In an environment of general mobility recovery, any week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility indicates growing public transport usage, which directly translates to higher foot traffic in retail and recreation areas over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases week-on-week by any amount
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat over the next 7 days, despite a week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility.
